subject: Integration kickoff: FinEdge SDK migration sprint
thread_summary: Kickoff coordination for FinEdge SDK onboarding: technical checklist, code samples, endpoint migration order, retries/timeouts guidance, and rate-limit handling. Action owners and a proposed 2-week cutover window.
messages:
From: Anna Ruiz <anna@finedge.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>; Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Brooks <tim.brooks@finedge.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Integration kickoff: FinEdge SDK migration sprint

Hi Hannah / Monica —

Thanks for making time. Were ready to start the SDK migration for FinEdges payments integration. Goals for the kickoff:
- Confirm final integration surface (authorization flow, webhooks, embeddings endpoint)
- Agree on endpoint migration order and any feature flags for graceful cutover
- Establish retry/timeouts and suggested rate-limit posture for the first 10k daily users
- Identify owners for sandbox -> prod cutover and a mutual action plan with dates

Attached: FinEdge-technical-requirements-v1.pdf (network diagrams + current timeout defaults).

Proposed window: 8/6 - 8/19 (two-week migration sprint) — flexible if Redwood prefers earlier.

Quick note on environment: well be running a hybrid of cloud and customer-hosted connectors; we need guidance on L7 timeout and reconnect behavior.

Can we set a 60m kickoff this week? Im available Thu 8/27 after 11:00 PT (open to earlier).

Thanks,
Anna Ruiz
Head of Integrations, FinEdge
anna@finedge.com
+1 415-555-0182

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Ruiz <anna@finedge.com>, Tim Brooks <tim.brooks@finedge.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Jul 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration kickoff: FinEdge SDK migration sprint

Anna — thanks for the clear brief and the doc. Happy to kick this off. Quick replies / proposals below: 

- Window: we can start earlier — proposed migration sprint: 8/1 - 8/14. If thats aggressive we can keep your 8/6 start.
- Kickoff: 8/27 sounds like a typo (I think you meant 7/27?). Im free Thu 7/27 11:00 PT; if not, Thu 7/28 09:00 PT also works.
- Owners: Ill act as overall CSM lead during the sprint. Monica will be your implementation PM and will own the sandbox->prod checklist and weekly sync.

Engineering guidance (high-level):
- Endpoint cutover order (recommended): 1) telemetry/webhooks (low risk), 2) embeddings endpoint (stateless), 3) auth/token rotation (stateful), 4) streaming/generation endpoints (final).
- Default timeouts: start with 10s connect, 60s read for generation calls; for long-running streams we recommend heartbeat pings and a 300s server-side keepalive.
- Retries: idempotent requests (health, status) = up to 3 attempts with exponential backoff starting at 200ms. Non-idempotent generation calls = client-side retry discouraged unless you tag requests with idempotency-key.

Ill attach sample snippets and a short checklist tomorrow (Monica will add implementation tasks).

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 27 Jul 2028 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration kickoff: FinEdge SDK migration sprint

Anna / Tim — jumping in with the implementation plan and concrete artifacts.

High-level sprint plan (2 weeks):
- Week 0 (pre-cut): sandbox access, API keys, sample app runbook, initial smoke tests
- Week 1: telemetry/webhooks + embeddings validation; parallel auth sandbox testing
- Week 2: staged cutover of streaming/generation endpoints and final reliability tests

Attachments Im uploading to the shared Drive: redwood-sdk-samples-v2.zip (go-to SDK snippets for node/python/go) and the sandbox access template.

Sample retry/timeout config we recommend for client teams (copy into your client config):
client.retry.maxAttempts=3
client.retry.initialBackoffMs=200
client.retry.maxBackoffMs=2000
client.timeout.connectMs=10000
client.timeout.readMs=60000
client.stream.keepaliveMs=300000

Notes:
- For embedding-heavy workloads, enable local batching and use Redis prefix caching for identical prompts. That keeps token costs down and reduces peak QPS.
- For migration, we suggest a traffic mirror for 48h before full cutover to compare latency and error rates.

Action items assign:
- Hannah: schedule the kickoff (owner)
- Monica: share SDK samples and runbook (owner)
- FinEdge (Anna/Tim): provide sandbox network allowlist + sample payloads (owner)

Let me know if you want a shorter pre-flight checklist; I can convert this into a 1-page runbook.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Implementation PM, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.ai

Quick operational notes from infra/serving: 

- Rate limits: for the first two weeks we recommend a soft QPS cap (via token bucket) of 120 QPS per customer with a 5% burst allowance. We can raise limits after stable telemetry for 48h.
- Endpoint migration order: follow Hannahs sequence. Important detail: when switching generation endpoints, 1) ensure KV cache warmup by replaying 1k synthetic requests in the staging environment, 2) enable prefix caching for high-frequency prompts to avoid cold-cache tail latency.
- Fallback policy: configure automatic fallback to an L3 cheaper model for 429s during the initial ramp; include circuit-breaker with 60s cooldown.

Sample policy snippet (for runtime routing):
routing.policies["finedge-gen"] = {
  primary: "r_gen_v2",
  fallback: "r_gen_v1_small",
  max_open_requests: 80,
  cooldown_seconds: 60
}

Ill join the kickoff and can demo the cutover checklist and a brief run through of the observability dashboard (latency, token costs, error budget).

Laura will own billing sync and will loop in Finance for any early overage approvals.

See you on the kickoff — Ill have the routing rules and a short slide ready.

Vivek Kulkarni
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
